title: Breakfast Nachos Supreme
subtitle: Tortilla chips loaded with eggs, bacon, cheese, and salsa on sheet pans.
description: Two sheet pans of loaded breakfast nachos feed ten fast: chips layered with queso, scrambled eggs, crisp bacon, pico, and avocado. Built in waves so the bottom layer stays crisp while the top gets melty and golden under the broiler.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Breakfast Nachos Supreme in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Bacon. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep components
steps.instruction: Cook bacon until crisp and crumble. Soft-scramble eggs—they should still look glossy. Warm nacho cheese. Drain pico thoroughly so chips don't sog out. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Layer the chips
steps.instruction: Spread chips on two rimmed sheet pans in a single thick layer. Drizzle half the nacho cheese, then scatter half the shredded cheeses over each pan. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: First melt
steps.instruction: Bake at 400°F until cheese melts and chips at the edges toast lightly. Remove and distribute scrambled eggs and bacon evenly across both pans. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Broil to finish
steps.instruction: Add remaining cheese and broil on high 2–3 minutes until bubbling and spotty golden. Watch constantly—chips burn fast under the broiler. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.instruction: Add pico, avocado, sour cream, and jalapeños immediately. Serve straight from the sheet pans at the line with extra hot sauce on the side. Plan about 2 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Build on two pans so the crew can attack from both ends of the table without a traffic jam.
Hold avocado and sour cream cold until the nachos leave the broiler—hot chips wilt them fast.
Serve within 5 minutes of broiling; nachos don't hold, so call the crew as soon as pans hit the counter.
cleanupNotes: Line sheet pans with foil for easier cleanup after melted cheese and queso bond to the metal.
Discard soggy bottom chips rather than scraping—foil lift-and-toss is faster on busy mornings.
leftovers: Nachos don't reheat well; repurpose leftover toppings into breakfast burritos with fresh tortillas.
Use extra scrambled eggs and bacon in a hash with diced potatoes for the next shift.
